title: Jets’ Aaron Glenn outduels Robert Saleh as New York’s defense stifles Titans
content:
The New York Jets’ new-look defense smothered the Tennessee Titans on Sunday, and Aaron Glenn beat his predecessor for the biggest victory of his tenure so far, a 23-10 win in Nashville, Tenn.

Facing former New York coach Robert Saleh, Glenn opened his second season as Jets coach with a win. Last season, New York did not get its first win until Week 8 and finished 3-14, with no victories by more than seven points. On Sunday, the Jets led 10-3 at halftime and scored on their first two possessions after the half to break it open. Despite a late Titans touchdown, the Jets finished with their largest margin of victory since Week 3 of 2024.

The Titans managed just 55 yards in the first half and 195 in the game, as second-year quarterback Cam Ward went 19-for-32 for 140 yards.

The Jets lost starting safety Minkah Fitzpatrick (groin) and first-round rookie wide receiver Omar Cooper (ankle) to injuries in the first half, and neither returned. Cooper was injured at the end of a 30-yard catch-and-run on the opening drive.

That answer is obvious, as the Jets won 23-10. But the bigger question is what it says about what these two teams have in front of them this season — and where they’re at right now.

On the Jets side of things: Glenn took over as the defensive play caller and clearly outclassed Titans offensive coordinator Brian Daboll — and that was even after losing a crucial piece (Fitzpatrick) to an injury early in the game. Glenn surprisingly barely blitzed, but he didn’t really have to. He had a secondary — arguably the biggest question mark on the roster — ready for everything Daboll and quarterback Ward threw at them, and the defense largely played with discipline in the passing game while dominating against the run. This is clearly a more talented, better-prepared defense than the one led by Steve Wilks last year — even if this will probably be the easiest offensive opponent the Jets will face for a while.

Saleh also called plays for Tennessee’s defense — which he didn’t do as the Jets’ head coach. That … didn’t go so well either. Frank Reich clearly out-coached him (more on that in a moment) and, most impressively, a talented Tennessee defensive line led by Jeffery Simmons didn’t make much noise at all against a Jets offensive line that had a very productive afternoon. The Jets drained the clock by pounding the ball in the running game, which helped put Geno Smith in position to make plays downfield and play with some level of efficiency. Saleh had nothing to throw at the Jets’ offense to disrupt them.

The Jets appear to be on the right track — or at least a better track than their opponent. The Titans will be mired in a greater rebuild than anyone (probably even Saleh) could’ve expected, considering some of the talent they have on both sides of the ball. Saleh still has a lot to prove when it comes to showing the Jets that, in his mind, they made a mistake firing him.

That feels like a ways away.

The Jets’ offensive coordinator hadn’t coached in an NFL game since the Carolina Panthers fired him as head coach midway through the 2023 season. The year before that, he was fired halfway through a season as the Colts’ head coach. Well, Reich made his return to the NFL in style — and his best series as play caller was the first. He most notably got rookie tight end Kenyon Sadiq — who missed most of training camp — involved in creative ways, including on a handoff to score a touchdown at the end of a scoring drive. The Jets’ third possession was a drawn-out, 19-play drive that ended with a field goal — though it could’ve ended in the end zone if not for a bad snap by center Josh Myers in the red zone.

The Jets killed most of the second quarter on a drive where they ran it 15 times but ultimately had to settle for a field goal after a false start and a Braelon Allen catch that was poked out by Titans linebacker Anthony Hill. Kicker Jason Sanders made a 33-yarder. A few possessions later, he badly missed a 54-yard attempt — which ultimately didn’t come back to bite New York.

The Jets started to pull away on another impressive drive in the third quarter that included a 40-yard bomb from Geno Smith to Adonai Mitchell — a duo that had plenty of chemistry in training camp — and ended with a Breece Hall scoring run and a 17-3 lead.

Reich out-coached Saleh all afternoon — an impressive feat considering the respect many have for Saleh’s defensive play-calling prowess, even during a failed Jets tenure.

Any hope the Titans had for the present — or the future — landed on the shoulders of the 2025 No. 1 pick. He showed some flashes of talent in an inconsistent rookie season, and the thought was that in a second year with a more stable environment, and under Daboll’s tutelage, he’d take a leap and look like a potential franchise quarterback.

It’s obviously early, but Ward’s performance — and Daboll’s — on Sunday did nothing to make any Titans fan believe he’s headed for anything special. Through three quarters, Ward had a -0.38 EPA per dropback against the Jets’ defense. For perspective: Brady Cook had a -0.38 EPA per dropback last season for the Jets, the worst mark among 42 qualifying quarterbacks. And it’s not as if it got any better in the fourth quarter, either, which included one sequence where Ward ran out of bounds on third down to take a sack from David Bailey, and another where he took a sack near his own end zone, nearly going for a safety. He finished the afternoon 19 of 32 for 140 yards and looked roundly unprepared.

Which gets to Daboll — he became the Giants’ head coach on a supposed reputation for play calling and developing Josh Allen in Buffalo. He won Coach of the Year with the Giants in 2022 after getting a career year out of Daniel Jones. It has been almost entirely bad since then, outside of some Jaxson Dart flashes last year. Sunday looked like more of the same from the worst parts of his Giants tenure, where he failed to exploit the easy, obvious weak spots in the Jets’ defense — specifically in the slot, where the Jets were banged up. The running game was stymied. And Daboll did nothing to make life easier for Ward.

This story will be updated.
